content:
Hi! I am currently working on a project called Metron (https://www.galois.com/project/metron) with Galois. We're trying to design robust and realistic benchmarks for AI targeting formal verification.

I can't talk about the details of what I'm designing, but I can say that I'm looking at problems in the Iris framework in Rocq. It's occurred to me that what with Iris-Lean rapidly maturing, it might be appropriate to adapt any such problems over to that too. Models are unliklely to be well-trained in that at all!

Does the Iris Lean community feel that the project is mature enough yet for such a thing? What is the dependency chain for Iris Lean; I think it has a reasonably light footprint? I am interested in your thoughts.

Cool! In terms of expressivity, I think we're mature enough to do benchmarks of this kind--a handful of us in this channel are already using Iris-Lean for new research. We are still smoothing out some latent performance bugs (Nikolai Zeldovich has submitted two in the past few days) and we'd love to hear anything you can tell us about running Iris-Lean on bigger proof experiments.

Our dependencies are Batteries and Qq.

Awesome. Honestly right now I'm still proving relatively small things - scaling up is tough as I do need to provide model solutions as part of problem creation. But it's great to hear you think the maturity is there. Batteries and Qq are quite modest so that's good.
